text: [Music]
what does fat do to your body you need
to eat a small amount of fat as part of
a balanced diet it provides essential
fatty acids and fat soluble vitamins
that keep your body working but fat is
high in calories 1 gram of fat contains
about double the calories found in 1
gram of carbohydrate or protein this
means eating too much fat can lead to
weight gain being overweight or obese
increases your risk of heart disease by
up to 28% even if you're otherwise
healthy the type of fat you eat matters
to the main types of fat in food our
saturated and unsaturated they have
different structures so behave
differently in your body too much
saturated fat is linked to increased
levels of bad non HDL cholesterol in
your bloodstream too much bad
cholesterol can increase your risk of
heart and circulatory disease fatty
deposits can build up in your arteries
and over time this can lead to symptoms
of angina or even a heart attack all
fats and oils contain saturated and
unsaturated fats we classify them based
on what they have most of coconut oil
ghee fatty meats and cheese contain
mainly saturated fat vegetable oils oily
fish avocados nuts and seeds contain
mainly unsaturated fat trans fat is
another type of fat it can raise on non
HDL cholesterol levels small amounts are
found in meat and dairy and trans fats
were added to foods in the past but now
UK manufacturers have removed this type
of fat from their products because of
this our intake of trans fats is now
below the recommended maximum Reference
Intakes our eyes give you an idea of how
much fat to eat they are a maximum not a
target the ri4 fat is 70 grams per day
one tablespoon of oil or enough spread
for one piece of bread are both around
10 grams of that 70 grams less than 20
grams should be saturated fat in the UK
most of us don't need too much fat
overall but we do eat too much saturated
fat swap saturated for unsaturated fat
to help lower your cholesterol swap
cheese for avocado swap fatty meat for
oily fish swap chocolate for unsalted
nuts compare food labels to make the
healthiest choice use oil instead of
butter lard or ghee for cooking and
measure it act every teaspoon of oil
adds 25 calories choose lean a meat such
as skinless turkey or chicken or have
pulses beans eggs or fish instead the
bhf is funding more research into fat
and how it affects your health find out
more at bhf dot org dot uk'
slash fats research
